speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Electricity Act was last amended in 2006, mainly to enhance the regulation and licensing of the transmission of electricity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Since then, the electricity sector has evolved with the increased proliferation of new technologies and business models.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There is a need to update the Electricity Act to ensure that it continues to remain effective and relevant amidst the changing energy landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Similar to the Gas (Amendment) Bill, in finalising these amendments, MTI and EMA sought feedback from industry stakeholders and members of the public through a public consultation in June earlier this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI and EMA have carefully considered all feedback received and incorporated them where relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I will now outline the key provisions of the Bill, starting with the first area of update, which is to enhance the security, reliability and competitiveness of electricity supplies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The transmission licensee operates the grid that transmits electricity generated by electricity generation licensees to consumers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: When installing new transmission infrastructure to meet electricity demand, the transmission licensee may, in certain situations, need to connect its electrical equipment to that of other electricity licensees, to increase transmission capacity and supply for the entire system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The direction will, in the first instance, require the transmission licensee and the electricity licensee to effect the connection and then agree on terms for maintaining the connection, including compensation to be paid by the former to the latter for loss suffered by the latter resulting from the connection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If both parties are unable to come to agreement on the terms, they can request the Minister to appoint an Appeal Panel under the Electricity Act to determine the terms, including compensation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The terms determined by the Panel will become effective and binding on both parties as an agreement from the date of the determination.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: EMA will also facilitate discussions to reach mutual agreement on the terms of connection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: A direction will only be issued if both parties cannot agree on the terms of connection despite these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The second amendment, in clause 3 of the Bill, amends the regulatory and licensing provisions in section 6 of the Electricity Act to enable the Minister to specify other electricity-related activities that need to be regulated and licensed, beyond the activities presently stated in that section.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This aligns with similar regulatory provisions already in the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The third amendment, in clause 8 of the Bill, will allow licensees to apply for a Judicial Management (JM) order under Part VIIIA of the Companies Act once EMA's consent is obtained.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Electricity Act currently prohibits an electricity licensee from applying for a JM.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While the intent is to ensure that critical licensees are not unilaterally placed under JM or dissolved, this restricts non-critical licensees from applying for a JM even though their restructuring or exit would not adversely impact our energy security and system stability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, this amendment allows JM of a licensee if EMA's consent is obtained.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is similar to the amendment to the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is currently not clearly stated in the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The fifth amendment, in clause 23 of the Bill, amends section 85 of the Electricity Act to rationalise the different offences currently provided in the section, which include offences relating to damage to land-based electricity transmission infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Such infrastructure is critical in ensuring the flow of electricity to businesses and households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The amendment also seeks to extend the reach of the section by making a person who causes or permits another person to damage land-based electricity transmission infrastructure guilty of an offence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There is no need for the former to have any particular relationship with the latter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is similar to the amendment to the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is in line with the penalty provided in the corresponding section in the Gas Act and will allow the Courts broader scope to determine appropriate penalties for such offences by considering such matters as the seriousness of the damage and its effects, and the circumstances in which the offence was committed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will better protect the interests of consumers when they engage firms to carry out electrical works at their homes or premises and enhance safety by ensuring that only licensed electrical workers are employed to carry out electrical works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clauses 9 to 14 of the Bill amend Part IVA of the Electricity Act to bring controls on ownership, acquisition and divestment over electricity licensees in line with those in the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This includes enabling the Minister to specify other electricity licensees as "designated electricity licensees" if the need arises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clause 21 of the Bill amends section 80 of the Electricity Act to harmonise the scope of duties of persons carrying out earthworks with those in the Gas Act, which are currently broader.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clause 29 of the Bill amends section 103 of the Electricity Act to enable EMA to recover costs for services provided in connection with its regulatory functions without having to prescribe the cost as fees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clause 28 of the Bill inserts a new section 100A to provide for various moneys collected by EMA under the Electricity Act to be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As the justifications for these amendments have already been mentioned in the Second Reading speech for the Gas (Amendment) Bill, I will only mention them briefly here.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, clause 16 of the Bill amends the Electricity Act to enable EMA to issue guidelines to signal to the market certain practices and conduct that are anti-competitive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It will also be an offence to do anything that compromises or affects the proper operation of a meter in duly registering electricity supplied to any person or premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These are similar to the amendments to the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Last, clause 27 of the Bill amends section 98 of the Electricity Act to enable regulations to be made to specify the procedures for submission of appeals to and consideration of appeals by the Minister regarding EMA's regulatory decisions, similar to the amendments to the Gas Act on this.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The massive power outage we experienced earlier this month is a reminder of how we should not take electricity for granted and how critical it is to secure and protect our power supply and transmission connections.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the event of a prolonged outage, these power sources will ameliorate hardships and reduce accidents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am aware that EMA is looking into the potential of micro-grids.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These are small electricity networks which are usually connected to a centralised national grid but that can also operate independently.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So far, these are only being tested at the Singapore Institute of Technology and Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In different parts of the world, the building of micro-grids is gaining momentum as governments realise their potential in adding to energy security.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They can be found in Amsterdam in The Netherlands, California and New York in the United States (US), Higashi Matsushima in Japan, just to name a few.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A network of small, independent electricity grids also offers an alternative in the event of cyberterrorism targeting the national grid.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the US, the Department of Homeland Security and the Federal Bureau of Investigation confirmed earlier this year that state-sponsored hackers had infiltrated the electricity grid.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A leading cybersecurity firm had also cautioned about cybercriminals posing a threat to utility operators.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hackers had caused an equipment shutdown at a Saudi Arabian oil and gas plant and a smelter in a German steel mill to overload and destroy itself.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to request that EMA draws up guidelines to guide staff on how to disseminate information and updates to the public in the event of outages.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During the recent blackout, hotlines were inundated and some people were unable to get their calls through.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Good communication is important in reducing anxiety and panic among members of the public who have no idea how long the outage would last.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is not easy for consumers to decide which electricity retailers to choose from.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Open Electricity Market is a very new concept for most Singaporeans and many of my elderly residents may get quite confused.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They cannot understand how a retailer can sell electricity at a more competitive price than the wholesale market.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MTI be able to provide them advisory services as this would be very useful for the senior citizens to make an informed choice?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We had discussed this earlier during the round-up speech for the Gas (Amendment) Bill and we very much agree that we can continue working on ways to improve by learning from best practices around the world, as well as experiences near and far.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As the Member rightly noted, microgrids can operate independently during an emergency.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: There is also an ongoing microgrid testbed at Pulau Ubin which is studying the real-world impact of renewable energy on grid system stability and reliability.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: These testbeds will provide useful insights to help EMA in planning for future grid designs, as well as the main grid to ensure resiliency.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We will continue to explore where such microgrids would be suitable for deployment in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As for cybersecurity threats to our electricity transmission system, I would like to assure the Member that the Electricity Act already gives EMA the mandate to address such threats, and EMA takes such threats very seriously.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For example, under the Electricity Act, EMA is able to go after persons who hinder or prevent the grid from being used or operated in the manner in which it is intended for.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Furthermore, the Computer Misuse and Cybersecurity Act also includes offences relating to cyberattacks or hacking, such as the unauthorised access to computers or computer systems, and unauthorised use or interception of computer services.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have also formulated a cybersecurity governance framework for the energy industry in close partnership with the Cyber Security Agency (CSA).

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The energy industry's Critical Information Infrastructures (CIIs) also adopt best practices in security management.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, for example, the computer systems in CIIs are isolated from the Internet.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In addition, there are regular industry-wide exercises and sharing sessions to ensure the sector's resilience and readiness in emergency responses to cyberattacks.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We will continue to work with CSA and the industry to ensure the robustness and relevance of our cybersecurity governance framework.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I will now address the Member's queries regarding contestability and the Open Electricity Market (OEM).

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Member asked about how the regulated tariff is determined and why retailers can charge less for their electricity packages.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The regulated tariff, charged by SP Group and approved by EMA, is set based on a fixed formula that reflects the long-term costs to produce and deliver electricity in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: SP Group is required to supply electricity to all consumers and has to bear the risk of an uncertain consumer base as it does not tie down its customers to any contract or impose early termination charges.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: On the other hand, retailers are able to set their prices based on their own business strategies to adapt to shorter-term factors, such as prevailing market conditions and level of competition.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We do share the Member's concern over ensuring that all households, including our senior citizens, and small businesses are able to make an informed choice on their electricity supplier.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: To this end, EMA uses regulatory measures, as well as community outreach.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As the regulator, EMA requires retailers to present and seek households' acknowledgement of the Consumer Advisory and Fact Sheet on the key contractual terms, such as payment terms, contract duration, security deposit and early termination charges.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: EMA also requires retailers to safeguard all security deposits collected from households.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For community outreach, EMA will also embark on education and awareness campaigns to inform consumers about the OEM and what to look out for when switching to a retailer.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As a consumer, you do not need to switch, there is no deadline to switch, and you can take time to consider your options and whether to switch.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The proposed amendment to the Electricity Act today also clarifies the right of small contestable consumers to revert to buying electricity at the regulated tariff, if they cannot, or do not, wish to purchase electricity from a retailer.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In summary, this Bill will ensure that the Electricity Act continues to remain effective and relevant in ensuring the safe and reliable supply of electricity, amidst the changing energy landscape.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.40 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.20 pm until 4.40 pm.
